text_blocks.snippet: A heart-healthy diet for diabetes focuses on balancing carbohydrates, proteins, and healthy fats while emphasizing fiber-rich foods and limiting processed foods and added sugars. It aims to manage blood sugar levels, improve cholesterol, and reduce the risk of heart disease, a common complication of diabetes.
snippet_highlighted_words: balancing carbohydrates, proteins, and healthy fats while emphasizing fiber-rich foods and limiting processed foods and added sugars

text_blocks.snippet: Key Components of a Heart-Healthy Diabetes Diet:

list.title: Prioritize Non-Starchy Vegetables:
list.snippet: Fill at least half of your plate with non-starchy vegetables like leafy greens, broccoli, and peppers.

list.title: Choose Whole Grains:
list.snippet: Opt for whole grains like brown rice, quinoa, and oats over refined grains.

list.title: Include Lean Protein Sources:
list.snippet: Incorporate fish (especially fatty fish like salmon), lean meats, poultry, beans, lentils, and tofu.

list.title: Healthy Fats:
list.snippet: Focus on unsaturated fats from sources like avocados, nuts, and plant-based oils (olive, canola, etc.).

list.title: Limit Processed Foods:
list.snippet: Minimize intake of processed meats, sugary drinks, baked goods, and other foods with added sugars and unhealthy fats.

list.title: Control Portion Sizes:
list.snippet: Be mindful of serving sizes to manage calorie intake and prevent weight gain.

list.title: Increase Fiber Intake:
list.snippet: Fiber-rich foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains help stabilize blood sugar levels.
Fatty fish: Salmon, tuna, sardines, and mackerel are rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which are beneficial for heart health.
Leafy green vegetables: Spinach, kale, and collard greens are packed with vitamins, minerals, and fiber.
Sweet potatoes: A good source of vitamin A, vitamin C, and fiber.
Berries: Strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries are rich in antioxidants.
Avocado: Contains healthy fats and fiber, and may help improve cholesterol levels.
Nuts: Almonds, walnuts, and other nuts provide healthy fats and fiber.
Yogurt: A good source of calcium, protein, and probiotics.
Oatmeal: A whole grain that is rich in fiber and other nutrients.
Saturated fats: Found in high-fat dairy products and animal proteins.
Trans fats: Found in processed foods and baked goods.
Added sugars: Found in sugary drinks, desserts, and many processed foods.
Sodium: Limit intake to manage blood pressure.

list.title: Hydrate:
list.snippet: Drink plenty of water.

list.title: Be Mindful of Eating Habits:
list.snippet: Eat slowly, pay attention to your body's signals of fullness, and avoid distractions while eating.

list.title: Regular Exercise:
list.snippet: Aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise most days of the week.

list.title: Consult a Healthcare Professional:
list.snippet: Work with your doctor or a registered dietitian to create a personalized meal plan that meets your specific needs and goals.
